item.title: Kenneth Walker powers Chiefs past Broncos in Kansas City debut
item.description: Kenneth Walker III ran 23 times for 173 yards and two touchdowns in his Chiefs debut, carrying Kansas City to a 31-10 win over Denver. Patrick Mahomes added two touchdown passes and a rushing score in his return from knee surgery as the Chiefs ended a three-game skid against the Broncos.

item.title: Kawhi Leonard returns to Toronto as Raptors-Clippers trade closes
item.description: Kawhi Leonard is headed back to the franchise he led to the 2019 NBA title. Toronto sent Brandon Ingram, Gradey Dick, two first-round picks, two second-rounders and a pick swap to the Clippers after the delayed deal cleared league review.

item.title: Judge homers as Yankees clinch record 61st postseason berth
item.description: Aaron Judge hit a three-run homer, his first since returning from a fractured rib that cost him more than three months, as New York beat Minnesota 8-3. The Yankees secured their ninth playoff appearance in 10 seasons and a major league-record 61st postseason berth.

item.title: Giants beat Cowboys 28-20 in John Harbaugh's debut
item.description: John Harbaugh opened his Giants tenure with the result New York hired him to deliver: a 28-20 win over Dallas. Jaxson Dart threw two touchdown passes to Isaiah Likely and another to Devin Singletary, while Cam Skattebo scored in his return from injury.

item.title: Alexander Zverev beats Ben Shelton for U.S. Open title
item.description: In a significant finish to Shelton's first major final, Alexander Zverev won 6-3, 7-6 (2), 5-7, 6-2 for his second Grand Slam championship. The result extends the long wait for an American men's major singles champion, which dates to Andy Roddick in 2003.

item.title: Men's tennis top 10 has no Big Three member for first time since 2002
item.description: Novak Djokovic fell from No. 5 to No. 12, leaving the men's top 10 without Djokovic, Roger Federer or Rafael Nadal for the first time since October 2002. Djokovic, 39, is the last of the era-defining trio still competing.

item.title: Texas erases 20-point fourth-quarter deficit to stun No. 1 Ohio State
item.description: The anticipated top-five matchup delivered a historic result: No. 4 Texas rallied from 23-3 down entering the fourth quarter to beat No. 1 Ohio State 24-23. Arch Manning led the comeback, capped by Hollywood Smothers' 1-yard touchdown with 25 seconds left. Sportradar called it the largest fourth-quarter comeback ever against an AP No. 1.

item.title: Elena Rybakina wins her first U.S. Open title
item.description: Elena Rybakina beat Aryna Sabalenka 6-4, 5-7, 6-2 for her first U.S. Open championship and third Grand Slam title. The victory denied Sabalenka a third straight Open crown and will lift Rybakina to No. 1 in the rankings.

item.title: Barry Melrose, hockey coach and longtime broadcaster, dies at 70
item.description: Barry Melrose, who coached Wayne Gretzky's Los Angeles Kings to the 1993 Stanley Cup Final before becoming one of hockey's most recognizable broadcasters, has died at 70. The former NHL player joined ESPN in 1996 and retired in 2023 after being diagnosed with Parkinson's disease.

item.title: Ben Shelton reaches first U.S. Open final
item.description: Ben Shelton beat Frances Tiafoe in four sets to reach his first Grand Slam final. He will face Alexander Zverev on Sunday with a chance to become the first American man to win a major singles title since Andy Roddick in 2003.

item.title: Rays and Brewers become first teams to clinch playoff berths
item.description: Tampa Bay and Milwaukee became the first MLB clubs to secure 2026 postseason spots. Junior Caminero's walk-off homer carried the Rays past Houston, while the Brewers clinched with a 20-0 rout of Cincinnati.

item.title: Ohio State visits Texas in early top-five showdown
item.description: No. 1 Ohio State visits No. 4 Texas Saturday night in the season's first top-five matchup. Julian Sayin and Arch Manning lead teams with national-title ambitions in a third consecutive meeting; the Buckeyes won the previous two.
